2. Leave was granted mainly on the ground that the High Court Division failed to apply the correct principle as to substitution of the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 as was applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 3. To recall briefly the facts of the case the predecessor of the appellants. Akhtar Banu, instituted Title Suit No. 9 of 1957 in the aforesaid Court for declaration of title to and for recovery and confirmation of possession in certain parts of the suit land. The suit on transfer to the 5th Court of the Subordinate Judge. Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 107 of 1959 and again on further transfer to the original Court was renumbered as Title Suit No. 245 of 1985. On 12-8-1969 the plaintiff came to know that defendant No. 4 had died and accordingly filed Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1969 on 28-8-69 for substitution of his heirs after setting aside abatement. The learned Subordinate Judge however suomotu recorded the abatement of the suit as a whole by his order dated 10-9-69 on account of the death of defendant No. 4. On 15-4-72 a lawyer of opposite party No. 3 (defendant No. 3) in the aforesaid misc. case informed the Court that the said opposite party had died on 4-4-72 whereupon the petitioner (plaintiff) prayed for time for substituting the heirs of the deceased opposite party No. 3. On 13-5-72 the learned Subordinate Judge passed the following order on the substitution petition filed by the plaintiff petitioner: "The OP files hajira, petitioner prays for substitution in place of deceased OP No. 3, on the grounds as stated therein. Heard, prayer is allowed. Let the heirs of the deceased OP 3 (be) substituted. Amend the plaint and the register accordingly. 

 4. The said misc case No. 25 of 1969 was dismissed on the ground of limitation with the observation that defendant No. 4 Md. Yakub had died on 29-1-65 and that abatement took place automatically when the legal representatives of the deceased were not brought on record within the prescribed time and no formal order was necessary. 

 5. The plaintiff preferred FMA No. 234 of 1976 in the High Court Division against the said order of the learned Subordinate Judge dismissing Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969. The appeal was allowed in part by judgment and order dated 29-7-81 holding that the suit did not abate as a whole but abated against defendant No. 4 only. In the said appeal, Feezza Khanum, (defendant No. 2) wife of deceased defendant No. 3 Aga Ali Reza appeared and the son and daughter of deceased-defendant No. 3 were also made parties in the appeal on the basis of their substitution in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969 and they also appeared in the said appeal. Defendant No. 1 filed CPLA No. 88 of 1982 and the aforesaid heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 filed CPLA No. 189 of 1982 against the aforesaid order of the High Court Division but the said petitions were is missed by this Division on 10-7-82. After the disposal of the leave petitions the record of the case was received by the learned Subordinate Judge on 6-12-83 and on the same day the heirs of the plaintiff (the present appellants) filed an application for substituting them in place of the plaintiff who had died on 20-9-83. The appellants did not file any petition for substitution of the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 Aga Ali Reza in the suit, in view of the fact that his wife, Feezza Khanum, defendant No. 2, was already on record and his son and daughter were substituted on 13-5-72 in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969. The appellants' prayer for their own substitution was allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 24-11-84. 

 6. On 12-12-84 defendant No. 1 filed a petition for recording abatement of the suit on account of non-substitution of the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 Aga Ali Reza. The appellants contested the said application by filing a written objection on 9-1-85 stating, inter alia, that the suit in any case could not abate as a whole. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 29-5-85 observed that the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 Aga Ali Reza having been substituted in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969 the question of abatement did not arise and the plaintiffs were directed to take necessary steps for substitution of the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3. Being aggrieved by the said order defendant No. 1 moved the High Court Division in revision in which the impugned judgment and order were passed. 

 7. It appears that a simple argument was made on behalf of defendant-respondent No. 1 in the High Court Division that the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3, who had died on 4-4-72, having not been substituted in the suit even within 90 days from 10-7-82 when the leave petitions were dismissed by this Division as referred to above the suit abated as a whole in view of the reliefs prayed for by the plaintiffs in the suit. On behalf of the appellants it was submitted that the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 having already been substituted in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969 it was not necessary for the plaintiffs to substitute the heirs of defendant No. 3 in the suit over again and that in any case the suit could not abate as a whole. 

 8. It is not disputed that the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 Aga Ali Reza were substituted in Mise, Case No. 25 of 1969, the wife of the deceased, Feezza Khanum, having already been on record as defendant No. 2. The learned Judge of the High Court Division took the view that the misc. case was a separate and independent proceeding and substitution made in that misc. case did not automatically substitute the heirs of deceased- defendant No.3 in the suit and that the plaintiffs ought to have taken steps for substitution of the heirs of the deceased-defendant after the abatement matter (on the death of defendant No. 4) was finally disposed of by this Division and the records came back to the original Court. The learned Judge has gone wrong in taking the aforesaid view and thus allowed himself to a wrong decision. 

 10. In the Privy Council case what happened was that in the course of the hearing of a suit in the Court of the District Judge, Ferozpur an application was made to the Chief Court of Punjab to revise an order of the District Judge directing the production of certain books. During the pendency of the matter in the Chief Court several of the parties died and substitutions were made in the proceeding in the Chief Court on ex parte applications. Then after the record when back from the Chief Court to the District Judge an application was made by one of the defendants for an order of abatement of the suit on the ground that the heirs of the deceased parties hat not been brought on the record of the suit within time. One District Judge ordered the abatement of the suit. A successor District Judge, however, set aside the order of abatement. The Chief Court set aside the latter order on the ground that a successor District Judge could not review an order of his predecessor. The Privy Council, however, allowed the appeal and remitted the case of the original Court to proceed with the hearing of the case on merit holding that in the circumstances no question of abatement arose. It is in this context that the Privy Council laid down the rule as aforesaid which is being followed consistently in the courts of the subcontinent including those of ours. 

 11. The Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of Ghulam Abbas Vs. Hashim 1969 SCMR 257 referred to the said rule and followed it. In that case substitution was made in the course of the appeal arising out of dismissal of the prayer for temporary injunction in the suit and the trial Court upon recommencing the trial after the disposal of the appeal ordered that the whole suit had abated because of non-substitution of the legal representatives of the deceased parties in the suit itself within time. The High Court in revision, however, set aside the order j of the trial Court not on the basis of the aforesaid rule but on a different ground. The Supreme Court  granted leave to consider whether the substitution  made in the court of appeal during the pendency of  the appeal from an interlocutory order would not ensure also for the purposes of the suit and be  sufficient to cure all defects in that behalf. Hamoodur Rahman, CJ in delivering the judgment noticed the  rule law down by the Privy Council and followed in  the Patna High Court in the case of Gobind Sahu vs. Zafar Karim AIR 1925 Pat. 145 and held that where legal representatives have already been brought on  the record in a connected and interdependent  proceeding, even though in a superior Court, it  would be hardly in keeping with this principle to insist upon a repetition of the process in a lower  Court. The question of abatement of the suit was thus held not to arise and the appeal was dismissed. 

 12. In the case before us the heirs of  deceased-defendant No. 3 having been brought on  record by substitution in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969  which arose out of the suit, the same was good  enough substitution of the heirs of deceased- defendant No. 3 for the suit itself and no further  application for substitution was necessary in the suit. The plaintiff is only required to file an application for correction by recording the names of the legal representatives of defendant No. 3 in the plaint and register. 

 13. It is regrettable that it was not even brought to the notice of the learned Judge that by the order of the Subordinate Judge dated 13-5-72 passed in Misc. Case No. 25 of 1969 (quoted hereinbefore) the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 were also ordered to be substituted in the suit itself. It was clearly stated in that order that let the heirs of deceased OP No. 3 (defendant No. 3) he substituted and the plaint and the register be amended accordingly. In view of this clear order as to substitution of the heirs of deceased-defendant No. 3 in the suit also, there was no requirement of a further application for substitution after the record was received back by the Subordinate Judge following disposal of the leave petitions in this Division. The abatement of the suit was wholly out of question. It appears that the learned Judge of the High Court Division wrongly decided the matter upon wrong submissions made by the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondent both on fact and law that the suit had abated. From the facts and law as noticed above it is clear that the suit did not abate in any case.
